effort-routing-1.measured_cost: No module in the medium run ever saw 1,524 in a tool result. CP-2A, CP-2G and CP-6 then received it in CP-2's handoff and confirmed it. High's CP-1A also read p.64 but did not use the figure. effort-routing-1.cause: The instructions sent to CP-1, CP-2, CP-2A and CP-2G never mention contractual obligations or scheduled or forward interest (grep: 0 hits in each). CP-2A's stress block (cpos_launch.py:1779-1789) anchors the interest shock only to 'a disclosed rate exposure'. So medium's 2.5-10% shock was a legitimate reading of the instruction. Whether a module finds the forward schedule depends on how much it happens to search.
effort-routing-1.proposal: Make it an instruction, not a matter of effort. (a) In CP-1's instructions, ask for a row with next-year scheduled interest payments from the contractual-obligations table, where the filing discloses one, or 'Not supplied: <reason>'. (b) Add one sentence to STRESS_BLOCK: where a forward interest schedule is stated, anchor the cash-interest increase to its step-up over base-period cash interest, or say why not.
effort-routing-1.estimated_saving: Not a direct saving. It makes the gain independent of effort, which is the precondition for keeping CP-3 and CP-6 at medium (−USD 0.44 per run against the balanced map, spliced from calls.jsonl) and possibly CP-2A (−0.19). Adding the row costs about 1 extra search per run (unmeasured, under USD 0.02).
effort-routing-1.quality_risk: Low, because it adds evidence. The risk is a module copying a schedule that rests on variable-rate assumptions without that limitation. The row's Basis must carry the issuer's rate assumptions, as high's CP-2 did (5.6-6.5%).
effort-routing-1.test_before_adoption: Answer key frozen from the 10-K before the rerun: the less-than-1-year scheduled interest is 1,524, and CP-2A's k is tied to 1,524/1,158. Rerun TDG all-medium with (a) and (b). Pass if CP-1 prints 1,524 with its rate assumptions, CP-2 states 4,173/1,524 = 2.74x, and CP-2A's interest shock cites the step-up. Repeat on one issuer whose filing has no contractual-obligations table and check that the row reads 'Not supplied'.

effort-routing-5.cause: Each module receives every upstream handoff whole in its first message (invocation.json, message 2: CP-5 577,598 characters, CP-8 708,317), and that first call is uncached. effort-routing-5.quality_risk: None from the measurement itself. The risk is misuse: treating shorter handoffs as better and pushing modules to drop evidence.
effort-routing-5.test_before_adoption: In the runs of finding 4, record each module's first-call input tokens per arm and check that the downstream increase follows the upstream word counts.

Budget._load counts any hold without a .settled marker as crash-left (src/deploy_workflow/model/budget.py:342, 414-415). (e) Start a second module only if cap - spent - reserved >= 2 x hold; otherwise run in order. The same filing pages are found again in each module: 34 of 101 (medium) and 55 of 126 (high) distinct pages were read by 2 or more modules. 10-K pages 144-153 (debt and liquidity) were read by 5-8 modules each.
tools-sources-5.cause: search_source is a case-insensitive exact-phrase match (handoff.py:420-440). Replaying every no-hit query with whitespace, dash, quote and NFKC normalisation produced 0 new hits. The rest are absent phrases (16 / 22), or the words occur on one page only by coincidence (checked examples: not adjacent). The misses come from guessed wording, not matching defects, so fuzzier search would not help. Every module rediscovers where the statements and notes are.
tools-sources-5.proposal: At source preparation, build a deterministic heading-to-page map for each filing: Items, financial statement titles and note headings, from the jsonl text. Return it with list_sources or the context (see tools-sources-4). Keep search_source unchanged.
tools-sources-5.estimated_saving: Hypothesis: a share of the USD 0.33-0.61 and 180-288 s of navigation calls. The size of that share is unmeasured.
tools-sources-5.quality_risk: A wrong or incomplete map could send the model to the wrong page. Search stays available, and the map adds no evidence of its own.
tools-sources-5.test_before_adoption: Offline: build the map from the retained jsonl and measure how many of the pages each module read in both runs fall under a mapped heading (target over 90%). Spot-check 20 headings against the filing. Then a paid run comparing navigation-only calls per module.

tools-sources-6.title: calculate cannot multiply, so CP-2G chains reciprocals across calls and leaves Decimal residues
tools-sources-6.measured_cost: Calls that only used calculate: 26 / 49, costing USD 0.48 / 1.38 and 273 / 958 s. Calls taking an earlier calculate result as an operand: 72 / 188 and 217 / 437. At high, CP-2G took 8 reciprocals (1/1.12, 1/0.5256 ...) and made 33 divide-by-reciprocal calls to multiply. That produced 7 residue values, e.g. 4674.0556799999999999999999999 where the exact product is 4674.05568. CP-2G high had 13 calculate-only calls, against 3 at medium.
tools-sources-6.cause: The calculate tool offers only 'sum' and two-operand 'ratio' (handoff.py:199-212). A product, or year-on-year compounding, takes a reciprocal call and then a division call, in sequence.
tools-sources-6.proposal: Add a 'product' operation to the existing Decimal-38 kernel: multiple operands, null for missing, same reason handling. No other change to the tool.
tools-sources-6.estimated_saving: At least CP-2G high's 3 reciprocal calls, and the compounding chain shortens (calls 5-8). Roughly USD 0.05-0.10 per high run (hypothesis). The larger gain is exact products with no residue.
tools-sources-6.quality_risk: New arithmetic code in a calculation path. It must keep exact lexemes and missing-versus-zero handling.
tools-sources-6.test_before_adoption: Property tests (hypothesis, pre-approved) comparing product against Decimal multiplication with an independent oracle, plus the retained CP-2G operands: 8892.8 x 0.5256 = 4674.05568 exactly. Mutation test the kernel change. Paid-run check that CP-2G's calculate-only call count falls.
